Most of the cost of healthcare is the cost of surviving once terminal illnesses. No one is making insane percentages of profit. In 1960, if you got cancer, it was pretty much a death sentence. Maybe they cut something out, but it was most likely too far gone by the time they found it. You got palliative care until you died.

There were no wonder drugs that cost hundreds of millions in R&D to develop, there were no MRIs, lasers, or genetic therapies. You had x-rays, surgery, antibiotics, and opiates.

If you got cancer - or any one of a number of other diseases - in 1960, you died and had (in 2016 money) a few thousand in medical bills.

If you get cancer - or any one of a number of other diseases - in 2016, you live, but you can have a few HUNDRED thousand in medical bills.

Twenty years ago leukemia was a death sentence, now something like 80% of leukemia can be cured with a pill - but someone spent a few hundred million making that pill, and if they don't get their money back, they won;t be able to make the next cancer curing pill. Science isn't cheap.

Need an MRI in Canada? Good fucking luck. You'll be waiting 6 months, and will have to drive hundreds of miles if you're in a rural area.

In 2007 a former Canadian Cabinet Minister went to California for breast cancer treatment, in spite of the fact that there was a cancer treatment center in her home riding named after her family because her father donated $8 million toward its construction.
